review.tagline: Text-to-speech model for dialogue, with laughter and pause control
review.summary: ChatTTS is a Python text-to-speech model trained for conversational speech in English and Chinese, with multi-speaker support and token-level control over laughter, pauses and interjections. It installs from PyPI, outputs 24 kHz audio, and ships a simple WebUI and command-line example. The released weights are a 40,000-hour pretrained model without SFT, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 for research use.
review.audience: Developers adding English or Chinese speech to LLM apps, for research use
strengths: Token-level prosody control: [laugh], [uv_break], [lbreak], plus sentence-level oral/laugh/break prompts
Random speaker sampling with saved embeddings for timbre recovery
Streaming generation and zero-shot inference code are included
Runs with about 4 GB GPU memory for a 30-second clip; RTF around 0.3 on a 4090
weaknesses: Model weights are CC BY-NC 4.0, academic use only; no commercial use
Only English and Chinese supported; English is described as experimental
Autoregressive output is unstable: speaker drift and quality vary between samples
Repo is the algorithm and examples; no packaged server or Docker image
needs: Needs PyTorch, torchaudio, vLLM (optional, Linux only)
